applied.fact: Which ledge the route starts from

pitch_detail.notes: Easy scrambling moves past flakes and a pruned tree, about 8 m up, gain a clean, slabby left-facing corner that leads to a two-bolt anchor. The approach ledge is a lower one; the highest ledge out of the gully leads to the start of P4 instead.

A few metres up the corner, make awkward moves over the roof onto the golden slab above. Zigzag past bolts, first left on crack features and then back right, pull a bulge, and follow thin crack features up and left. The moves after the bulge are thin and sustained; easier ground leads to the anchor. Graded 5.10+ to 5.10d.

Up the left-facing corner past flakes and a bolt, then step right to a second bolt and pull into the upper left-facing corner. Sustained and technical with finicky gear, to a two-bolt anchor at a large ledge. Walk the belay left 10–15 m along the ledge to a cairn at the start of P4. Given as 5.11 to 5.11c.
Another left-facing, slabby corner to a bolt, then face moves right past steep, flexing flakes and a solid layback flake. Pull around the arete to the right to the anchor.
A thin, technical finger corner leads into the big cave, Tiger Belly's Lair; the anchor is on the right side of the cave. Sustained and stout for its grade, which is given from 5.11- to 5.11a.

Traverse right out of the cave, clip a bolt, and climb a steep wall on positive holds, trending slightly right to a stance below the leaning roof. The Eye of the Tiger variation (5.12c/5.12+) climbs the orange corner straight out of the cave for about 40 m and rejoins the route above; accounts differ on whether it rejoins after P7 or P8.

The crux: follow the exposed, stepped roof leftward past two bolts, alternating strenuous underclings with holds above the lip. At the end of the roof (a BD #2 fits), reachy but easier moves past a pin reach the anchor. Grades given are 5.12- to 5.12b.

A short, steep, strenuous layback in the left-facing corner past a fixed piece and two bolts, then a rest on a stance. From a bolt, hand-traverse left past another bolt, with poor feet at first, onto the slab and a sloping belay. A second two-bolt anchor about 7 m up and right is off route.

Straight up cracks and flakes until you can trend left on twin thin cracks, balancy and protected by two fixed nuts. An easier ramp leads left to the anchor at the base of the Tiger Flake. Given as 5.11 to 5.11b.

Clip the bolt left of the anchor and make committing moves to a small ledge, then undercling and jam left around the giant Tiger Flake and continue to its final steep, wide section. Keep a BD #5 for after the first section, to protect the follower, and a #6 for the end. Manage the rope carefully; belay on a big ledge.

Broken cracks and blocky features lead up and right to a final bulge and onto the ridge; anchor from a tree. The weakest pitch on the route. Descend by rappelling the route with two ropes, including diagonal rappels, or by the third-class ramp on the left side of the wall.
